items.text: Saints WR Chris Olave is active (expected to play after hamstring designation).
items.why: Confirmed active; Schefter and Rap earlier expected him to play with no setbacks.
items.implication: WR1 role intact; no docks needed.

items.text: Bengals QB Joe Burrow, listed as questionable, is officially active vs. the Texans.
items.why: Official inactive list confirmation after expected-to-play reports.
items.implication: Full QB1 projection unlocked; Bengals pass game elevated.
items.opportunity: Normal snap share and red-zone looks expected.

items.text: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (cracked rib) practiced Friday, improved steadily, team did not elevate WR; optimism he can go, pushing to play.
items.why: Bullish tone; flak jacket if plays; official likely ~2:30pm/90-min window.
items.implication: Project in with docks; high-upside if full.
items.opportunity: Primary target share if active; else Quentin Johnston rises.

items.text: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) downgraded to OUT; opens door for Rashod Bateman.
items.why: Saturday downgrade confirmed; inactive reports Sunday.
items.implication: Ravens WR targets redistribute; Bateman/Andrews elevated.

items.text: Steelers have downgraded WR Michael Pittman Jr. to OUT with foot injury.
items.implication: PIT WR room thins; slot/YAC options rise.
items.opportunity: Elevated looks for Roman Wilson/Germie Bernard types.

items.text: Nico Collins (hamstring) ruled out for Week 2 (context with Flowers/Bowers).
items.why: Official ruled out per multiple reports.
items.implication: HOU WR targets to Hutchinson/Noel/Boutte; Schultz TE bump.

items.text: Projecting Ladd McConkey in with decent injury docks; RapSheet tone bullish, official status likely until 2:30pm ET. Puka true GTD. Olave clean/no docks. Decent look at Jonah Coleman (Harvey doubtful) and Germie Bernard (Pittman out).
items.why: Player-specific docks and beneficiary identification from ETR summary + Rap tone.
items.implication: DFS/season-long adjustments; McConkey startable with risk, Olave full go.
items.opportunity: Coleman/Bernard volume spikes; McConkey limited efficiency possible.

items.text: Weekend FF reports summary: GTD McConkey (optimism+flak) & Nacua (hip); not expected Harvey; expected Olave/Burrow/Black/McMillan (snap count); OUT Flowers & Pittman.
items.why: Consolidated Sunday AM beat/insider reports for slate.
items.implication: Core status board for start/sit and projections.

items.text: Rams consider WR Puka Nacua (hip), listed questionable for MNF vs Giants, a pre-game decision.
items.why: Missed practices; true GTD per ETR/Levitan/Berry.
items.implication: Have pivot ready for MNF; true uncertainty.
items.opportunity: If out: heavier TE usage (Ferguson/Parkinson) + Konata Mumpfield/Malachi Fields bump; Whittington also doubtful.

items.text: Broncos RB R.J. Harvey (hamstring), listed questionable, is unlikely to play vs Jaguars.
items.why: Source report Sunday AM; ETR not expected.
items.opportunity: Decent look expected for Jonah Coleman or committee mates.

items.text: Raiders elevated TE Chris Myarick with Brock Bowers doubtful (knee); could return next week.
items.opportunity: Michael Mayer targets elevated (led last week in absence).

items.text: Loves Kenneth Walker vs IND: 21/24 RB touches (74% snaps), 40% route targets (team lead); IND gave 163 yds/3 TDs to Henry. Utilization smash.
Loves Ashton Jeanty @ LAC: 99 utilization (tied Bijan lead), 19% target share last 10; 25+ touches 3/4 recent. Soft LAC D.
Loves Bucky Irving vs CLE: RB9 util, 26% target share, 100% RB RZ touches; CLE soft vs run (121 yds/4.8 YPC).
Loves Justin Jefferson @ CHI: 37% target share from Wentz Wk1; 93 yds/18 PPG career with Wentz; CHI soft vs WRs.
Hates Travis Etienne @ BAL: matched Miller rushes Wk1, most pts via air; Kamara expected back squeezes role further; underdog script.
Hates Marvin Harrison Jr. vs SEA: only 8% target share Wk1 (5th on team), zero RZ; SEA tough vs WRs.
Loves Dak Prescott vs WAS (smash home spot, high total, WAS torched); Dalton Kincaid vs DET (top-5 TE util, high routes, DET soft vs TEs).
